AI infrastructure economics are increasingly defined by the cost of producing intelligence rather than acquiring computing capacity. As inference demand outpaces training growth, infrastructure providers and their customers must increase productive computing time without a corresponding rise in operating costs. The emergence of continuously learning agents and physical AI applications is further complicating that equation.
